subject: Re: Request: SDLC control package — CI/CD & secrets governance
messages:
From: Laura Park <laura.park@secure-assess.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: controls@clearwaterbank.com
Date: 2028-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Intake: SDLC controls for SIG/SOC2 evidence collection

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this on. Clearwater is running a targeted intake for SDLC controls focused on CI/CD gating, secrets handling, and change management. To close our scope we need the following artifacts and short answers by EOD Feb 14:

- A control matrix that maps PR approval -> build -> deploy with owners and evidence locations.
- CI pipeline runbook showing where ephemeral credentials are used and how they rotate.
- A brief note on secrets at rest vs in-flight (KMS/HSM integration, redaction).
- Any exceptions or temporary allowances to the standard flow in the last 12 months.

If you can share a redacted policy and an attachment index, we can mark items as reviewed quickly. Also happy to take a 30-min walkthrough on Feb 14 if you prefer a screen share.

Laura Park
Senior Controls Assessor
Secure Assess LLP

[Attachment: intake_checklist.csv (CSV)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Park <laura.park@secure-assess.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-10T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intake: SDLC controls for SIG/SOC2 evidence collection

Laura — thanks for the clear scope. We're on it. Quick summary of what I'll attach and where to find things in the Drive link below:

1) control matrix (sdlc_control_matrix.xlsx) — maps PR -> CI job -> canaries -> prod rollout, includes owners and sample evidence references (PR numbers, pipeline runs).
2) ci_pipeline_runbook.pdf — describes job authentication, ephemeral runner behavior, broker tokens, and rotation cadence.
3) redacted_kms_policy.txt — high-level KMS key usage and access list (redacted service account ids).
4) exceptions.log — short list of change-window exceptions in the past 12 months with approvals.

Two quick notes to call out so you don't need to dig:
- We use ephemeral runner credentials for third-party contribution builds; tokens are minted with 15m TTL and rotated by the build orchestrator (section 3.2 in the runbook).
- PR gating requires at least two approvers for code owners paths and a passing ephemeral-scanning job (SCA + secret-scan). If a job is flaky we have a documented fallback (described in the runbook).

I'll attach the redacted files to this thread and put the full index in the Drive folder. If Feb 14 works for a walkthrough, propose 10:00–10:30 PT.

Jordan Blake
Senior Security Engineer — Platform
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: sdlc_control_matrix.xlsx (XLSX); ci_pipeline_runbook.pdf (PDF); redacted_kms_policy.txt (TXT)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Park <laura.park@secure-assess.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-11T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intake: SDLC controls for SIG/SOC2 evidence collection

Jordan — small clarification request from Laura's list that might require a short note: for the ephemeral runner flow, do we perform key attestation on the runner host before provisioning tokens (e.g., TPM or instance identity)? Also, can we provide the last rotation timestamp for the signing key used by our deploy pipeline?

I can pull the attestation step diagram and the rotation timestamp from the key vault logs, but want to confirm the level of redaction they need (full principal names vs redacted service ids). Laura — what is your preference?

Irene
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Park <laura.park@secure-assess.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intake: SDLC controls for SIG/SOC2 evidence collection

Laura — attaching the redacted artifacts and answers below. Thanks for the flexibility on redaction; we kept service principals obfuscated but included timestamps and audit IDs you can use to verify logs.

Quick answers inline:
- Attestation: yes — we require instance identity (cloud metadata attestation) and a lightweight host integrity check before the broker mints short-lived tokens; see runbook section 3.2. Attestation flow diagram: attached.
- Signing key rotation: last rotation recorded 2027-12-18T03:26:12Z (Key ID: redacted-K-1123, audit ref: AUD-20271218-74). Full rotation history is in the key vault audit export (shared via Drive link).
- Exceptions: two temporary elevated-change windows in the last 12 months (listed in exceptions.log) — both approved by the change board; approval IDs included.

I've uploaded the full index and a short 30-slide walkthrough deck to the Drive folder and included a DocuSign link for the confidentiality acknowledgement you requested. Confirming our walkthrough slot: Feb 14, 10:00–10:30 PT works for us.

Jordan Blake
Senior Security Engineer — Platform
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: attestation_diagram.png (PNG); exceptions.log (TXT); pipeline_signing_rotation.csv (CSV)]
